The Babylonians came to her to sleep with her and defiled her with their prostitution. She was defiled by them, and she became disgusted with them.
She exposed her prostitution and uncovered her nakedness. Then I turned away from her in disgust, just as I had turned away from her sister.
She increased her prostitution and remembered the days of her youth, when she prostituted herself in the land of Egypt.
She attached herself to their servants, whose genitals were like those of a donkey and whose emissions were like those of horses.
You revisited the wickedness of your youth, when you were deflowered in Egypt and your youthful breasts were fondled.
Therefore, Oholibah, this is what the Lord of lords says: I am stirring up against you all your lovers with whom you became disgusted, and I will bring them against you.
They will surround you: the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Put, Lud, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them, desirable warriors, lords and rulers, all of them men of Kedar riding steeds.

They will come against you armed, with chariots, wagons, and multitudes of peoples. They will surround you with spears, shields, and helmets. I will place judgment before them, and they will judge you according to their judgments.

I will turn my jealousy against you. They will break your nose in fury and tear off your ears. Those left of you will fall by the sword. They will take away your sons and daughters, and those left of you will be consumed by fire.
They will take your splendid ornaments and strip off your clothes.
I will put an end to your scheming and to your prostitution from the land of Egypt. You will not lift your eyes toward them, and you will no longer remember Egypt.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am handing you over to those you hate, to the Assyrians, from whom you turned away in disgust.
They will strike you in their hatred, take everything you have worked for, and leave you naked and bare. The shame of your prostitution and your wickedness will be exposed.
These things will be done to you because of your prostitution, because you prostituted yourself by pursuing the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.
Because you walked in your sister’s ways, I will put her cup into your hands.
This is what the Lord of lords says: You will drink your sister’s cup, deep and wide, and you will become an object of great and utter laughter and mockery.
You will be filled with drunkenness and sorrow—a cup of horror and destruction, the cup of your sister Samaria.
You will drink it and drain it. You will cut off your hair and cut off your breasts, for I have spoken, says the Lord of lords.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Because you have forgotten me and thrown yourself after your idols, you too must bear your wickedness and your prostitution.
The Lord said to me: Mortal, judge Oholah and Oholibah, and show them their defilement.
For they have committed adultery, and there is blood on their hands. They have committed adultery with their idols, and they burn in the fire the children they bore to me.
This is another thing they did to me: they defiled my sanctuary that very day and profaned my Sabbaths.
When they slaughtered their children for their idols, they entered my sanctuary that very day and defiled it. This is what they did inside my house.

They also sent for men to come to them from far away, men to whom they had sent messengers. When the men arrived, they immediately bathed, painted their eyes, and adorned themselves with their ornaments.
They sat on covered couches, and tables were arranged before them. They took my oil and my incense for themselves.
The sound of their rejoicing went out, along with that of the men who had come from Sheba and from the wilderness. They put bracelets on their hands and splendid crowns on their heads.
And I said, “For with these, and with the deeds of prostitutes, they practice prostitution.”
They went in to them as men go in to a prostitute. That is how they went in to Oholah and Oholibah, women who were prostitutes.
Righteous men will judge them as adulteresses and as women who shed blood, because they are adulteresses and there is blood on their hands.
For this is what the Lord of lords says: Bring an assembly against them and hand them over to terror and plunder.
The assembly will stone them, and they will strike them with their swords. They will kill their sons and daughters and burn their houses with fire.
I will put an end to wickedness in the land. All women will be warned and will not practice prostitution as you have.
I will bring your prostitution back upon you, and you will bear the sins of your idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to me in the ninth year, on the tenth day of the tenth month, saying:
Son of man, write down the date of this day, this very day on which the king of Babylon laid siege to Jerusalem.
Tell a parable about the rebellious house and say to them: This is what the Lord of lords says: Set the pot on and pour water into it.
Put into it good, fatty cuts of meat, a shoulder with its bone removed,
from the choicest of the flock. Stoke the bones beneath the pot and burn them underneath it.
For this is what the Lord of lords says: O city of bloodshed, in which the pot has been set and whose wickedness has not left her! Cut her up limb by limb, and let no lot fall upon her.
For her blood was within her, and she put it on a rock. She did not pour it out on the ground, so that dust would not cover it.
To stir up wrath for vengeance, I put her blood on a smooth rock so that it would not be covered.
Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: O city of blood! I myself will make the woodpile large.
Heap up the wood and kindle the fire. Let the meat cook, bring it to a boil, and let the bones burn.
Set it boiling on the coals, so that its bronze becomes hot and melts, its filth dissolves within it, and its punishment is completed.
Like diseased figs, the abundance of her wickedness will not go out of her. Rather, her punishment will be by fire.
Because you defiled yourself with prostitution, and because I cleansed you but you were not cleansed of your filth, you will not be cleansed again until I have spent my fury on you.
I, the Lord, have spoken. I will bring it about and do it. I will not relent, spare, or show mercy. I will judge you according to your ways and your deeds, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, look, I am taking away from you the delight of your eyes with a sudden blow. Do not mourn or weep, and do not shed tears.
But groan silently for the dead, and do not hold a mourning gathering. Fasten your clothes around you and put your sandals on your feet. Do not cover your lips, and do not eat the bread people bring.
I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening. The next morning I did as I had been commanded.
The people said to me, “Will you not explain to us what this is that you are doing?”
I said to them, “The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Say to the house of Israel: This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am defiling my sanctuary, the glory of your strength, the delight of their eyes, and what your souls cherish. Your sons and daughters whom you have left behind will fall by the sword.
You will do as I have done. You will not cover your lips, and you will not eat the bread of other people.
Your hair will not be cut, and your sandals will remain on your feet. You will not weep or mourn. You will waste away in your wickedness and console one another.
Ezekiel will be a sign to you. You will do just as he has done, and you will know that I am the Lord of lords.
But you, son of man, on the day when I take from them their strength, the joy of their glory, the delight of their eyes, what their souls cherish, and their sons and daughters—
on that very day a survivor will come to you and bring the news to your ears.
On that day the survivor will open your mouth, and you will speak and no longer be silent. You will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am the LORD.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, turn your face toward the Ammonites and prophesy against them.

Say to the Ammonites, “Hear the word of the Lord of lords. This is what the Lord of lords says: Because you said, ‘Aha!’ over my sanctuary when it was defiled, over the land of Israel when it was devastated, and over the house of Judah when they went into captivity,

therefore, look, I am giving you to the people of the east as an inheritance. Their army will settle among you, and they will pitch their tents among you. They will eat your fruit and drink your milk.
I will make Rabbah a resting place for camels and the land of the Ammonites a resting place for sheep. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Because you clapped your hands, stamped your feet, and rejoiced with all your heart over the land of Israel,

therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am raising my hand against you. I will give you to the nations as plunder, wipe you out from among the peoples, destroy you from among the countries, and leave you in ruins. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Because Moab and Seir said, ‘Look, the house of Judah is like all the nations,’
Therefore, look, I am laying bare the flank of Moab, stripping it of its cities, its cities and their surrounding areas, the glory of the land: Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim.
I will give it as an inheritance to the people of the east and the Ammonites, so that Rabbah of the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations.
I will execute judgment on Moab, and you will know that I am the Lord.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Because Edom took vengeance on the house of Judah, committed a great wrong, and raged against them,

therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am raising my hand against Edom. I will destroy its people and livestock and make it a wasteland from Teman and Dedan [?]. It will fall by the sword.
I will carry out my vengeance on Edom through my people Israel. They will take vengeance on Edom according to my anger and my fury, and they will know my vengeance, says the Lord of lords.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Because the Philistines acted in vengeance and took revenge with the desire of their hearts to destroy an everlasting friendship,
therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am raising my hand against the Philistines. I will destroy the Cretans and destroy the remnant along the seacoasts.
I will exact great vengeance on them with rebuke and anger. They will know that I am the LORD when I exact my vengeance on them.
In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, because Tyre said about Jerusalem, “Aha! The gates of the peoples are broken, and they have turned toward me. She has been devastated and laid waste,”
therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against you, Tyre. I will bring many nations up against you, as the sea rises with its waves.
They will destroy Tyre’s walls and pull down her towers. They will remove her soil from her, and I will make her like a smooth rock.
She will become a place for spreading fishing nets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, says the Lord of lords. She will become plunder for the nations.
Her daughter towns in the countryside will be killed by the sword, and they will know that I am the Lord.

For this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am bringing Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, against Tyre from the north, with horses, chariots, horsemen, an assembled army, and a great multitude.
He will kill your daughter settlements in the countryside with the sword. He will set up siege towers against you, lay ambushes against you, and erect barriers against you.
He will drive the points of his lances into your walls, and they will tear down your towers with their swords.

The movement of his horses will cover you with dust. Your walls will shake at the sound of his horsemen and the wheels of his chariots when he enters your gates like someone entering a city whose walls have been breached.
With his horses’ hooves he will trample all your streets. He will kill your people with the sword and pull your lofty strongholds down to the ground.
They will plunder your possessions and carry off your property. They will pull down your walls and demolish your splendid houses. They will throw your stones, timber, and wealth into the sea.
I will put an end to the abundance of your songs, and the sound of your lyre will no longer be heard.
I will make you a smooth rock and a place for spreading fishing nets. You will never be rebuilt, for I have spoken, says the Lord of lords.
This is what the Lord of lords says to Tyre: At the sound of your fall, at the agony of your slain, and at the slaughter taking place within you, the islands will tremble.

All the rulers of the sea will come down from their thrones, remove their robes, and take off their splendid clothes. They will clothe themselves in terror and sit on the ground. They will tremble without rest and be appalled at you.

They will raise laments over you and say to you, “How you have perished, you who inhabited the seas, the mighty city that was powerful on the sea, you and your inhabitants! All your inhabitants have been shattered.”
Now the islands will tremble on the day of your downfall, and the islands will be thrown into turmoil on the day of your downfall.
This is what the Lord of lords says to Tyre: “When I make you a ruined city, like cities that are uninhabited, I will bring the deep up over you, and great waters will cover you.

I will bring you down with those who descend into the pit, to the people of ancient times. I will make you dwell in the land below, among the ancient ruins, with those who descend into the pit. You will not be inhabited, and I will not establish you in the land of the living.”
I will hand you over to destruction. You will be sought, but you will never again be found, says the Lord of lords.”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
“But you, son of man, raise a lament over Tyre.
Say to Tyre, which sits at the entrance to the sea and trades with the peoples and many islands: “This is what the Lord of lords says: Tyre, you said, ‘I am the crown of glory.’
Your borders are in the heart of the seas, and your builders perfected your beauty.
They brought you ribs and planks from Senir, and they took cedars from Lebanon to make masts for you.
They made your oars from the oaks of Bashan, and they made your decking of elephant ivory from the islands of Kittim.
They brought embroidered coverings of fine linen from Egypt to serve as your banner. They brought you blue and purple cloth from the islands of Elishah for your covering.
The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; your wise men, Tyre, were your sailors.
The elders of Gebal and its skilled men were in you, repairing your leaks. All the ships of the sea and their sailors were among those who traded with you.
Persians, Lydians, and men of Put, warriors, were in your armies. They hung shields and helmets in you and brought you glory.
The men of Arvad and your troops stood on your walls and guarded your towers. They hung their shields all around your walls and made your beauty complete.
Tarshish was your trading center and a source of your abundant wealth. They brought you silver, iron, tin, and lead to sell.
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your merchants, trading in human beings and bronze vessels.
From Beth-togarmah they brought you horses, horsemen, and mules for sale.
The sons of Daran [?] were your merchants, and many islands were markets for your goods. They brought you horns of oil and frankincense as gifts.
Edom was your trading center because of the abundance of your products. They brought you purple cloth, fine linen, embroidered cloth, blue cloth, silk, and [?] to sell.
Judah and the land of Israel were your merchants. They brought you wheat, rice, millet, honey, oil, and balm to sell.
Damascus was your trading center because of the abundance of your products and your abundant wealth, trading in rich wine and white wool.
Dan and Javan from Uzal brought you goods to sell. They brought you iron for you to work, wood, and reeds to sell.
Dedan was your trading center. They brought you an abundance of choice livestock.
They also brought you rams, lambs, and young goats.
The merchants of Sheba and Raamah brought you choice spices, precious stones, and gold for sale.
Haran, Canneh, and Eden, the merchants of Sheba, and Assyria were your trading centers.
These were your merchants, who brought you blue and embroidered garments and valuable treasures, bound with ropes and carried in ships of [?] wood.
The people of Tarshish among your trading partners brought you cargoes, and you became full and very strong.
Those who handled your oars brought you into the heart of the seas, into great waters. A scorching wind shattered you in the heart of the seas.

Your wealth and the earnings from your trade, all your warriors and your sailors, those who repaired your leaks from among your trading partners, all your warriors, and the whole company within you will fall into the heart of the seas on the day of your downfall.
At the sound of your seafarers’ wailing, those around you will tremble.
All who handle oars will come down from their ships, along with the sailors and all the seamen, and they will stand on the land.
They will wail over you with loud and bitter wailing. They will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes.
They will shave their heads for you, wrap themselves in sackcloth, and weep bitterly over you with mourning dances.
Their sons will raise laments over you and say, “What city was ever like Tyre, which sat in the midst of the sea?
When your goods came out of the sea, you satisfied many peoples. With your abundant wealth and trade, you enriched the kings of the earth.”
When you were shattered and fell into the depths of the sea, your merchandise and your entire company fell within you.
All the inhabitants of the islands were appalled at you. Their kings trembled, and their faces streamed with tears.
The merchants of the peoples hissed at you. You have come to destruction and will be no more forever.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre, “This is what the Lord of lords says: Because your heart has become proud and you have said, ‘I am God, and I sit on God's throne in the heart of the seas’—yet you are a human being, not God, though you consider your heart to be like God's heart—
Are you perhaps wiser than Daniel, or have you seen hidden things through your wisdom?
With your understanding you have acquired wealth for yourself and gathered silver and gold into your treasuries.
Through your great wisdom and your trade, you have increased your wealth, and your heart has become proud because of your wealth.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Because you have considered your heart to be like the heart of God,
look, I am bringing foreigners against you, mighty men of the nations. They will draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom and defile your splendor.
They will bring you down to the pit, and you will die the death of those slain in the heart of the seas.
Will you really say before those who kill you, ‘I am God’? For in the hands of those who kill you, you are a human being, not God.”
You will die at the hands of uncircumcised foreigners, for I have spoken, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, raise a lament over the king of Tyre and say to him: Thus says the Lord of lords: You were the seal of likeness, full of wisdom and a crown of glory.

You were in Eden, the paradise of God, and you were adorned with every precious stone: sardonyx, carbuncle, emerald, beryl, sapphire, jasper, crystal, and pearls. You filled your treasuries with gold and your storehouses with precious stones from the day you were created.
You were with the anointed cherub who shelters, and I placed you on God's holy mountain. You were among the stones of fire.
You walked blamelessly in your ways from the day you were created until wrongdoing was found in you.

Through your extensive trade, you filled your inner being with wrongdoing and sinned. I struck you down from the mountain of God, and the sheltering cherub destroyed you from among the stones of fire.
Because your heart became proud of your beauty, your wisdom was corrupted along with your beauty. I threw you to the ground before kings and made you a spectacle for them.

Through the abundance of your [?] and the wrongdoing of your trade, you defiled your sanctuary. I will bring fire out from within you, and it will consume you. I will turn you to ashes on the ground before the eyes of everyone who sees you.
Everyone among the peoples who knows you will be appalled at you, because you will come to destruction and will be no more forever.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, turn your face toward Sidon and prophesy against her.

And say: Thus says the Lord of lords: Look, I am against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in you. They will know that I am the Lord when I carry out my judgments in her and show my holiness in her.
I will send a plague upon her and blood into her streets. Her slain will fall within her by the sword that surrounds her, and they will know that I am the Lord.
No longer will the house of Israel suffer bitter thorns and disfiguring pain from all those around them who treat them with contempt. They will know that I am the Lord of lords.

Thus says the Lord of lords: When I gather the house of Israel from the nations among whom they were scattered and show my holiness through them before the eyes of the nations, they will live in the land that I gave to my servant Jacob.

They will live there peacefully, build houses, and plant vineyards. They will live confidently when I execute judgments against all the nations around them that harass them. They will know that I am the Lord their God.
In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth day, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, turn your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.
Speak and say: Thus says the Lord of lords: Look, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon lying among the rivers, who says, 'The river is mine, and I made it.'
I will put a bridle in your jaws and make the fish of your river cling to your scales. I will pull you up out of your river, and all the fish of your river will cling to your scales.

I will throw you into the wilderness, you and all the fish of your river. You will fall on the open field and will not be gathered or collected. I have given you as food to the wild animals and the birds of the sky.
All the inhabitants of Egypt will know that I am the Lord, because you were like a reed staff to the house of Israel.
When they grasped you with their hands, you pierced their hands. When they leaned on you, you broke and made their backs tremble.
Therefore, thus says the Lord of lords: Look, I am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy both people and livestock from among you.
The land of Egypt will become a ruin and a wasteland, and they will know that I am the Lord, because you said, 'The river is mine, and I made it.'
Therefore, look, I am against you and against your river. I will make the land of Egypt a ruin and a wasteland, from Migdol of Syene to the border of Cush.
No human foot will pass through it, nor any hoof of livestock, and it will remain uninhabited for forty years.

I will make the land of Egypt a ruin among desolate cities, and her cities will lie ruined for forty years among devastated cities. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them among the cities.
Thus says the Lord of lords: After forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the nations among whom they were scattered.
I will bring back the captives of Egypt and settle them in the land of Pathros, in the land from which they were sold. There they will be a lowly kingdom.
It will be lower than all the kingdoms and will no longer rise above the nations. I will make them few, so that they cannot subjugate the nations.
They will no longer be a source of hope for the house of Israel or a reminder of the wrongdoing of following after them. They will know that I am the Lord of lords.
In the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon subjected his whole army to hard labor against Tyre. Every head became bald, and every shoulder was rubbed bare. Yet neither he nor his army received wages from Tyre for the labor he performed against it.

Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am giving the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will take its possessions, carry off its captives, and plunder its spoils, and it will be wages for his army.
In return for the work he did against Tyre, I have given him the land of Egypt, says the Lord of lords.
On that day I will make a horn rise for the house of Israel, and I will open your mouth among them. Then they will know that I am the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, prophesy and say: This is what the Lord of lords says: Wail and say, ‘Alas for the day!’
For the day is near; the day of the Lord is near—a day of clouds and a time for the nations.
The sword will come against Egypt, and there will be terror in Cush when the slain fall in Egypt, when they take away its wealth and tear up its foundations.
The Cushites, the people of Put, the Libyans, all Arabia, Cub, and the people of the land of the covenant will fall with them by the sword.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Those who support Egypt will fall, and its mighty strength will be broken. From the tower of Syene they will fall within it by the sword, says the Lord of lords.
They will lie in ruins among ruined lands, and their cities will be among ruined cities.
They will know that I am the Lord when I set fire to Egypt and all her helpers are shattered.
On that day messengers will go out hurriedly from my presence to destroy Cush, which lives at ease. There will be turmoil among them on Egypt’s day. Look, it is coming!
This is what the Lord of lords says: I am handing over Egypt’s wealth to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,
Him and the mighty men of the nations who come to destroy the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.
I will bring the rivers to ruin and hand the land over to the wicked. I will devastate the land and everything in it through foreigners. I, the Lord, have spoken.
This is what the Lord of lords says: I am destroying the idols and putting an end to the objects of worship in Memphis. There will no longer be a ruler in the land of Egypt.
I will lay waste the land of Pathros, set fire to Zoan, and carry out judgment on No.
I will pour out my fury on Sin, Egypt’s stronghold, and destroy the wealth of No.
I will set fire to Egypt. Sin will be thrown into turmoil, No will be breached, and Memphis will fall.
The troops of Pi-beseth will become like water. They will fall by the sword and go into captivity.
At Tahpanhes the day will grow dark when I break Egypt’s scepter there and the glory of its strength comes to an end. A cloud will cover it, and its daughters will go into captivity.
I will carry out judgment on Egypt, and they will know that I am the Lord.
In the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. It has not been bandaged so that it might heal. No poultice will be placed on it, and it will not be bandaged or grow strong enough to hold a sword.
Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will break his strong arms and make the sword fall from his hands.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them among the countries.
I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put my sword in his hands. He will cut off Pharaoh’s arms, and Pharaoh will groan before him with the groans of the slain.

I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but Pharaoh’s arms will fall. They will know that I am the Lord when I put my sword in the hands of the king of Babylon and he draws it against the land of Egypt.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them among the countries. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, say to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and to his forces: Whom do you resemble in your greatness?
Look, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches, dense shade, and great height. Its top was among the thick foliage.
The waters made it grow, and the deep made it tall. Its planting spread around the rivers, and it stretched its branches over all the trees of the field.
Therefore it grew much taller than all the trees of the field. Its boughs multiplied and its branches grew long because of the abundant waters that made it grow.
All the birds of the sky nested in its branches, and all the wild animals gave birth beneath its boughs. Many nations lived in its shade.
It was beautiful in its greatness and its many branches, because its roots were in abundant water.
The cedars in the garden of God did not surpass it. The fir trees could not match its branches, and the plane trees were not like its boughs. No tree in the garden of God matched its beauty.
I made it beautiful with its many branches, and all the trees of Eden, the garden of God, envied it.
Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: Because it grew tall, its top shot up among the thick foliage, and its heart became proud because of its height,
I will hand it over to the mighty ruler of the nations. He will deal with it according to its sin and destroy it.

foreigners, the mighty men of the nations, will destroy it and cast it down on the mountains. Its branches will fall in all the valleys, and its boughs will be broken in all the ravines of the land. All the nations of the earth will come down from its shade and abandon it.
When it falls, all the birds of the sky will settle on it, and all the wild animals will be beneath its boughs.

This is so that none of the trees by the water will exalt themselves in their height or send their tops up among the thick foliage, and none of those that drink water will stand up or become like them. For they have all been handed over to death, to the earth below, among the human beings who go down to the pit.

This is what the Lord of lords says: On the day it went down to Sheol, I brought about mourning. I covered the deep on its account, restrained its rivers, and held back the abundant waters. I made Lebanon mourn over it, and all the trees of the field fainted.

The earth shook at the sound of its fall. When I brought it down to Sheol with those who go down to the pit, all the trees of Eden, the choice and beautiful trees of Lebanon that drink water, were comforted in the earth below.
They too went down with it to Sheol, to those killed by the sword. Its offspring had lived in its shade among the nations.

Which of the trees of Eden could compare with you in glory and greatness? Yet you have gone down with the trees of Eden to the earth below. You will lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword. This is Pharaoh and his entire army, says the Lord of lords.
In the eleventh year, in the twelfth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, sing a lament over Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say to him: You compared yourself to a lion among the nations, but you are like a sea monster. You thrashed about in your rivers, muddied the water with your feet, and trampled their rivers.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am spreading my net over you with a gathering of many peoples, and they will haul you up in my net.
I will throw you onto the ground and cast you down in the open field. I will make all the birds of the sky settle on you, and I will fill all the wild animals of the earth with your flesh.
I will cast your flesh onto the mountains, and the valleys will be filled with your carcasses.
I will drench the land of your watchtowers with your blood, and the mountains and valleys will be filled with you.
When you are extinguished, I will cover the heavens and darken their stars. The sun will be covered with clouds, and the moon will not give its light.
I will darken over you all the lights that shine in the heavens, and I will bring darkness over your land, says the Lord of lords.
I will anger the hearts of many peoples when I bring your destruction among the nations and into countries you do not know.
I will make many peoples appalled at you, and their kings will be afraid when I flash my sword before them. On the day of your downfall, they will fear and tremble, each for his own life.
This is what the Lord of lords says: The sword of the king of Babylon will come against you.
With the sword of warriors I will bring down your might and that of all the mighty ones of the nations. They will plunder Egypt’s strength, and all her wealth will be plundered.
I will destroy her livestock beside the abundant waters. No human foot will muddy them again, nor will the hoof of an animal.
Then I will make their waters settle and make their rivers flow like oil, says the Lord of lords.
When I make the land of Egypt a ruin, and the land is laid waste with everything in it, when I strike down all its inhabitants, they will know that I am the Lord.
This is a lament, and the daughters of the nations will sing it. Over Egypt and all her wealth they will sing it, says the Lord of lords.
In the eleventh year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, sing a lament over Egypt’s army, and bring it down with her among the mighty nations, to the earth below, with those who go down to the pit.
“Go down from pleasant waters and lie down with the uncircumcised.
“They will fall among those killed by the sword, and they will drag him away with his entire army.
The rulers of the nations will speak with their troops from within Sheol. They will go down and lie uncircumcised with those killed by the sword.
“Assyria is there, with its entire company around its grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword.
They made his grave in the depths of the pit, and his company was around his grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword, because they caused devastation in the land of the living.

Elam is there, with her entire army around his grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword. They went down uncircumcised to the earth below because they caused devastation in the land of the living, and they bore their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

Among the slain they made a bed for him, in the midst of his army. Around his grave are all the uncircumcised who were killed by the sword because they caused devastation in the land of the living. They bore their disgrace with those who go down to the pit, and they were counted among the slain.
Meshech and Tubal are there, with her entire army around his grave, all of them uncircumcised, killed by the sword because they caused devastation in the land of the living.

They will not lie with the fallen warriors among the uncircumcised who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, whose swords were laid beneath their heads, and whose guilt rested upon their bones, because in their might they caused devastation in the land of the living.
“But you will lie among the uncircumcised and rest with those killed by the sword.
Edom is there, with her kings and all her princes, who, despite their might, were counted with those killed by the sword. They will lie with the uncircumcised and with those who go down to the pit.

The rulers of the north are there, and all the Sidonians, who went down with those killed by the sword, ashamed and broken despite their might. They lay uncircumcised with those killed by the sword, and they bore their shame with those who go down to the pit.
Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over his entire army, those killed by the sword—Pharaoh himself and his entire army, says the Lord of lords.
For I brought about his destruction in the land of the living, and I made him lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword—Pharaoh himself and his entire army, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, speak to your people and say to them: When I bring the sword against a land, the people of that land are to take one man from among them and appoint him as their watchman.
When he sees the sword coming against them, he must blow the horn and warn the people.
“whoever hears the sound of the horn and does not heed the warning, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head.
“But if he heeds the warning, he will save his life.

But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the horn or warn the people, and the sword comes and takes a life from among them, that person is taken away because of their sins, but I will hold the watchman accountable for their blood.
But you, son of man, I have appointed as a watchman for the house of Israel, to hear a word from my mouth and warn them on my behalf.

When I tell a wicked person, ‘You will certainly die,’ and you do not tell that wicked person to beware of his ways, that wicked person will die in his wickedness, but I will hold you accountable for his blood.
But if you warn the wicked person to turn from his ways and he does not turn, he will die in his wickedness, but you will have saved your own life.
But you, son of man, say to the house of Israel, ‘This is what you have said: Our wickedness and our sins weigh upon us, and we are wasting away because of them. How can we live?’

Say to them, ‘As I live, says the Lord of lords, I take no pleasure in the death of a wicked person, but rather that the wicked person should turn from his wickedness and live. Repent and turn away from your evil ways, so that you do not die, house of Israel.’

But you, son of man, say to your people, ‘The righteousness of a righteous person will not save him on the day he sins, and a wicked person will not stumble because of his wickedness on the day he turns from his wickedness. Nor will a righteous person live on the day he sins.’

When I tell a righteous person that he will certainly live, but he trusts in his righteousness and afterward does wrong, none of the righteousness he has practiced will be remembered in his favor. Instead, he will die because of the wrong he has done.
And when I tell a wicked person, ‘You will surely die,’ but he turns away from his sins and practices justice and righteousness,
If he returns the pledge he took, repays what he took unjustly, follows the commandments that give life, and does no wrong, he will certainly live; he will not die.
none of the sins he has committed will be remembered against him. Instead, he will live because of the justice and righteousness he has practiced.
Yet your people say, ‘The Lord’s way is not right.’ It is their own ways that are not right.
When a righteous person turns away from his righteousness and does wrong, he will die because of his wrongdoing.
And when a wicked person turns away from his wickedness and practices justice and righteousness, he will live because of them.
Yet you say, ‘The Lord’s way is not right.’ I will judge each of you according to your ways, house of Israel.
In the eleventh year of our captivity, on the fifth day of the tenth month, someone who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me and said, ‘The city has been destroyed.’

Before the escaped man came to me, the hand of the Lord had been upon me in the evening, and he opened my mouth by the time the escaped man came to me in the morning. Once my mouth was opened, it was no longer shut.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, those who live in these ruins in the land of Israel say, ‘Abraham was only one man, yet he inherited the land. We are many; will we not inherit it?’
Therefore say to them, ‘This is what the Lord of lords says: You eat meat with the blood, lift your eyes to your idols, and drink blood, yet you want to inherit the land!’
You rely on your swords, practice defilement, and each of you defiles his neighbor’s wife, yet you want to inherit the land!

Say to them, ‘This is what the Lord of lords says: As I live, all who are in the ruins will fall by the sword. All who are in the open country I will give to the wild animals for food, and all who are in the clefts and caves will die of plague.’
I will make the land a ruin and a horror. Its proud strength will come to an end, and the mountains of Israel will be desolate, with no one passing through.
They will know that I am the Lord when I make the land a ruin and a horror because of all the defilement they have practiced.

But you, son of man, your people talk about you beside the walls and at the doors of their houses. They speak to one another, each to his brother, saying, ‘Come and hear what message has come from the Lord.’
The people come to you and sit before you. They hear your words but do not act on them, because deceit is in their mouths, and they follow the thoughts of their own hearts.
They regard you as a song, as a beautiful voice, and as a sweet-sounding harp. They hear your words but do not act on them.
But when your words come to pass, then they will know that you are a prophet among them.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Prophesy and say to them, the shepherds, ‘This is what the Lord of lords says: O shepherds of Israel who feed themselves! Should not shepherds feed the flock?’
You eat the fat animals, clothe yourselves in their wool, and slaughter the fattened animals, but you do not feed the flock.
You have not strengthened the weak, healed the sick, bandaged the injured, brought back the straying, or searched for the lost. Instead, you have subjected them to force.
My sheep were scattered because they had no shepherd, and they became food for all the wild animals.
My flock wandered over all the mountains and on every high hill. My flock was scattered over the whole earth, with no one searching for them or gathering them.
Therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord.

As I live, says the Lord of lords, because my flock became plunder and food for all the wild animals for lack of a shepherd, and the shepherds did not tend my flock, but instead the shepherds fed themselves and did not feed my flock—
therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord.

This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against the shepherds! I will hold them accountable for my flock and stop them from tending my flock any longer. I will rescue my flock from their mouths, and they will no longer be food for them.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I myself will seek out my flock and care for them.
As a shepherd looks after his flock on a stormy day, so I will look after my sheep and gather them from all the places where they were scattered on the day of clouds and thick darkness.

I will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the countries. I will bring them into their own land and pasture them on the mountains of Israel, in the valleys, and in all the inhabited places of the land.
I will feed them in good pasture, and their fold will be on the high mountains of Israel. There they will lie down in a good fold and graze on rich pasture on the mountains of Israel.
I myself will pasture my flock, and I myself will make them lie down, says the Lord of lords.
I will seek the lost, bring back the straying, bind up the injured, and strengthen the sick. I will protect the fat and the strong, and I will shepherd them with justice.
But as for you, my sheep, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am judging between one ewe and another, and between one ram and another.
Is it not enough for you shepherds to graze on good pasture, that you also trample the rest of your pasture with your feet? You drink the water, but muddy with your feet what you leave over.
My flock grazes on what your feet have trampled and drinks the water your feet have muddied.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the weak sheep.
Because they were pushing with their sides and shoulders and thrusting with their horns at all the weak sheep, until they were scattered outside,
I will save my sheep, and they will no longer be plunder for them. I will judge between one ewe and another, and between one ram and another.
I will appoint a shepherd over them to pasture them—my servant David. He will pasture them, and he will be their shepherd.
I, the Lord, will be their God, and my servant David will be ruler among them.
I will establish a covenant of peace with them and remove dangerous wild animals from the land. They will live peacefully in the wilderness and sleep in the forest.
I will give them my blessing around my hill. I will send down rain in its season, and it will be rain of blessing.

The trees of the land will bear fruit, and the land will yield its crops. They will live securely in their land, and they will know that I am the Lord when I break their yoke and rescue them from the hands of those who enslaved them.
They will no longer be plunder for the nations, nor will wild animals devour them. They will live securely, with no one to frighten them.
I will establish a planting of peace for them. They will no longer suffer from famine in the land, and they will no longer endure the scorn of the nations.
They will know that I am the Lord their God, and that they, the house of Israel, are my people, says the Lord of lords.
You, my sheep, the sheep of my pasture, are human beings, and I am the Lord your God, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, turn your face toward Mount Seir and prophesy against it.
Say to it: This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against you, Mount Seir. I will raise my hand against you and make you a ruin and an object of horror.
I will turn your cities into ruins, and you will be devastated. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
Because you maintained an everlasting hostility and handed the Israelites over to the sword in the time of their distress, at the time of their final wrongdoing,
therefore, as I live, says the Lord of lords, I will give you over to bloodshed, and bloodshed will pursue you. The bloodshed you hated—that very bloodshed will pursue you.
I will make Mount Seir a ruin and a horror, and I will destroy from it those who pass through and those who return.
I will fill its mountains with its slain. Those slain by the sword will fall on your cliffs, your hills, and in your valleys.
I will make you a ruin forever, and your cities will not be inhabited. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
Because you said, ‘These two nations and these two kingdoms are mine, and I will take possession of them,’ even though the Lord was there,
therefore, as I live, says the Lord of lords, I will deal with you according to the anger and hostility with which you acted and hated them. I will reveal myself among them when I judge you.
You will know that I am the Lord. I have heard all the insults you spoke against the mountains of Israel, saying, ‘They are devastated, and they are ours to devour.’
You opened your mouths wide against me and multiplied your words against me, and I heard.
This is what the Lord of lords says to Mount Seir, which dwells amid the joy of the whole earth: I will make you a wasteland.

Because you rejoiced that the inheritance of the house of Israel was devastated, I will do the same to you. You will become a ruin, Mount Seir, together with all of Edom. And they will know that I am the Lord.
And you, son of man, prophesy concerning the mountains of Israel and say to the mountains of Israel: Hear the word of the Lord of lords.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Because the enemy said about you, ‘Aha!’ and said, ‘The ancient heights are ours as a possession.’

Therefore prophesy and say: This is what the Lord of lords says: Because you have been dishonored, devastated, and reviled by those around you, and have become the possession of the remaining nations, and have become the subject of gossip and the talk of the nations,

therefore hear the word of the Lord of lords, mountains of Israel. This is what the Lord of lords says to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, to the deserted ruins and abandoned cities that have become plunder and an object of ridicule for the remaining nations around them:

Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: In the fire of my jealousy I have spoken against the remaining nations and against all Edom, because they made my land their own possession. With joy in their hearts they humiliated people, to take them captive and plunder them.

Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel, and say to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys: This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I have spoken in my jealousy and my fury, because you have endured the insults of the nations.
Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: I have raised my hand against the nations around you, declaring that they will bear their own disgrace.
But you, mountains of Israel, will put out your branches and produce abundant fruit for my people Israel, because they will soon come.
Look, I am turning toward you, and you will be cultivated and sown.
I will multiply people upon you, the whole house of Israel. The cities will be inhabited, and the ruins will be rebuilt.

I will multiply people and livestock upon you, and they will increase and become numerous. I will make you inhabited as in former times, and I will do good to you as at the beginning. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
I will cause people, my people Israel, to walk upon you. They will possess you, and you will be their inheritance. You will never again be bereaved.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Because they say to you, ‘You devour human beings and bereave her people,’
from now on you will not devour human beings, and you will no longer bereave your people, says the Lord of lords.
I will no longer let the insults of the nations be heard against you. You will no longer endure their contempt, and you will no longer bereave your people, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, the house of Israel lived in their land and defiled it with their ways and their deeds. Their conduct before me was like the uncleanness of a menstruating woman.
I poured out my anger upon them because of the blood they shed in the land, and because they defiled it with their idols.
I scattered them among the nations and dispersed them among the cities. I judged them according to their ways and their deeds.
They went among the nations and profaned my holy name. The nations said of them, ‘These are God's people, yet they have left his land.’
I had concern for my holy name, which the house of Israel had defiled among the nations to which they went.

Therefore say to the house of Israel: This is what the Lord of lords says: I am not acting for your sake, house of Israel, but for the sake of my holy name, which you profaned among the nations to which you went.

I will show the holiness of my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, which you profaned among them. The nations will know that I am the Lord, says the Lord of lords, when I show my holiness through you before their eyes.
I will bring you out from the nations, gather you from the countries, and bring you to your own land.
I will sprinkle clean water on you and cleanse you from all your uncleanness and from all your idols.
I will give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will remove the heart of stone from your bodies and give you a heart of flesh.
I will put my Spirit within you and cause you to follow my commandments and to keep my judgments and carry them out.
You will live in the land that I gave your ancestors. You will be my people, and I will be your God.
I will save you from all your uncleanness. I will summon the grain and make it plentiful, and I will not bring famine upon you.
I will increase the fruit of the trees and the crops of the land, and you will no longer suffer the disgrace of famine among the nations.
There you will remember your evil ways and your detestable deeds, and your faces will be drawn with shame over your wrongdoing and your defilements.
Know that I am not doing these things for your sake, says the Lord of lords. Be ashamed and let yourselves be turned from your evil ways, so that you do not die, house of Israel.
This is what the Lord of lords says: On the day when I cleanse you from all your wrongdoing, I will make the cities inhabited and rebuild the ruins.
The land that was ruined will be cultivated, though it had lain desolate in the sight of everyone who passed by.
They will say, ‘That desolate land has become like the garden of Eden, and the cities that were ruined and demolished have become strong fortresses.’
The nations remaining around you will know that I, the Lord, rebuild what has been demolished and plant the desolate places. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will do it.
This is what the Lord of lords says: I will again seek out the house of Israel in this matter, to act on their behalf, and I will multiply them like a flock of people.
Like a consecrated flock, like the flocks of Jerusalem at the time of its festivals, so the cities that were ruined will be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
The hand of the LORD was upon me, and the LORD brought me out by his Spirit and set me down in a valley. It was full of bones.
He led me around among them, and I saw that there were very many in the valley, and they were very dry.
He said to me, “Son of man, can these bones live?” I said, “You know, Lord of lords.”
He said to me, “Prophesy over these bones and say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD.
This is what the Lord of lords says to these bones: Look, I am bringing breath into you, and you will live.
I will put sinews upon you, make flesh grow upon you, and cover you with skin. I will put breath within you, and you will live. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
I prophesied as he commanded me. As I prophesied, there was a noise and a shaking, and the bones came together, each bone to its joint.
And I saw tendons and flesh grow over them, and skin covered them on top, but there was no breath in them.

And he said to me, “Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and say to the breath: ‘This is what the Lord of lords says: Come, breath, from the four winds, and breathe into these slain people so that they may live.’”
I prophesied as he commanded me, and breath entered them. They came to life and stood on their feet, an exceedingly great army.
And he said to me, “Son of man, all these bones belong to the people of Israel, who were saying, ‘Our bones have dried up, our hope has perished, and we are finished.’”
“Therefore prophesy and say to them: ‘This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am opening your graves and bringing you up from your graves, and I will bring you to the land of Israel.’”
You will know that I am the Lord when I open your graves and bring you up from your graves.
“I will put my spirit in you, and you will live. I will settle you in your land, and you will know that I am the LORD. I have spoken, and I will act, says the Lord of lords.”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“But you, son of man, take one stick and write on it, ‘Judah and the people of Israel associated with him.’ Take another stick and write on it, ‘Joseph, on the stick of Ephraim, and all the people of Israel associated with him.’”
Bring them together, one beside the other, so that they become one stick in your hand.
If your people say to you, ‘Tell us what these things mean,’

“Say to them: ‘This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am taking the stick of Joseph, which is in Ephraim’s hand, and the tribes of Israel associated with him. I will put them together with the stick of Judah and make them one stick, and they will be one in my hand.’”
Hold the sticks on which you write in your hand before their eyes.
“And say to them: ‘This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am taking the people of Israel from among the nations to which they went. I will gather them and bring them to their land.’”
“I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king will rule over them all. They will no longer be two nations, nor will they again be divided into two kingdoms.”

“They will no longer defile themselves with their idols, their impurities, or any of their wrongdoing. I will rescue them from all the places where they lived and sinned, and I will cleanse them. They will be my people, and I will be their God.”
“My servant David will reign over them, and they will all have one shepherd. They will follow my laws, keep my commandments, and carry them out.”

“They will live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob, where their ancestors lived. They, their children, and their children’s children will live there forever, and my servant David will be their ruler forever.”
“I will establish a covenant of peace with them, and it will be an everlasting covenant with them. I will increase their numbers and place my sanctuary among them forever.”
My dwelling will be among them, and they will be my people.
The nations will know that I am the Lord who makes Israel holy, when my sanctuary is among them forever.’”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
“Son of man, turn your face toward Gog and toward the land of Magog, the ruler and chief of Meshech and Tubal. Prophesy against him and say:”
‘This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against you, Gog, ruler and chief of Meshech and Tubal.

“I will gather you, put a bridle in your jaws, and bring you out of your land—you and your entire army, horses and horsemen, all of them wearing armor, a great assembly with spears and shields, all wielding swords.”
All the Persians, Cushites, and people of Put are with them, with shields and helmets.
“Gomer and all its army, Beth-togarmah and the farthest parts of the north and all their armies, and many peoples with you.”
Get ready, you and your entire assembly gathered with you, and be their guard.

“You were appointed from ancient days, and in the latter years you will come against the mountains of Israel and against a land that has found peace after the sword and has been gathered from many peoples. All of them will live there in peace.”
“You will come up like a storm, like a cloud covering the land—you, your entire army, and the many peoples with you.”
“This is what the Lord of lords says: On that day thoughts will arise in your mind, and you will devise an evil plan.”
“You will say, ‘I will go up against a prosperous land and attack those who live in peace, who have no walls, bars, or gates.’”

“To take captives and seize plunder, you will turn your hand against the ruins that have been resettled and against a people gathered from the nations, who have acquired livestock and possessions and live in the finest part of the land.”

“Sheba and Daran [?], the merchants of Tarshish, and all the towns will say to you, ‘Have you come to take captives and seize plunder? Have you gathered your forces to carry away silver and gold, take livestock and possessions, and lead away a great number of captives?’”
“Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog: ‘This is what the Lord of lords says: On that day, when my people Israel live in peace, you will know.’”
“You will come from your place, from the farthest parts of the north, with many peoples, all riding horses, a great assembly and a vast army.”

“You will come up against my people Israel like a cloud covering the land. In the latter days you will come, and I will bring you against my land so that the nations may know me when I show my holiness through you before their eyes.”

This is what the Lord of lords says: Are you the one I spoke about in former days through my servants, the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in those days and during those years that I would bring you against them?
On that very day, when Gog comes against the land of Israel, says the Lord of lords, my anger will burn in my fury.
In my zeal, in the fire of my anger, I have declared that on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.

The fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the wild animals, every crawling creature that crawls on the earth, and all human beings on the face of the earth will tremble before him. The mountains will be overturned, the towers will fall, and all the walls will fall to the ground.
I will summon a sword against him throughout all my mountains, says the Lord of lords. Each man's sword will be against his brother.
I will judge him with death and bloodshed. I will pour down torrential rain, hailstones, fire, and sulfur on him, on his commanders, and on the many peoples with him.
I will show my greatness and my holiness before the eyes of many nations, and they will know that I am the LORD.
And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: This is what the Lord of lords says: I am against you, Gog, ruler and chief of Meshech and Tubal.
I will subdue you, gather you, bring you up from the far reaches of the north, and bring you to the mountains of Israel.
I will strip your bow from your left hand and your arrow from your right.
You will fall on the mountains of Israel, you and your entire army and the many peoples with you. I have given you as food to the winged birds and the animals of the earth.
You will fall in the open country, for I have spoken, says the Lord of lords.
I will send fire upon Magog and upon the inhabitants of the islands who live peacefully, and they will know that I am the Lord.
I will make my holy name known among my people Israel, and I will no longer profane my holy name. The nations will know that I am the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
Look, the day of which I spoke is about to come, says the Lord of lords.
The inhabitants of the towns of Israel will go out and set fire to the weapons, shields, javelins, bows, arrows, hand clubs, and spears. They will use them as fuel for seven years.

They will not need wood from the fields or the forest, but will use their weapons as fuel. They will take captive those who took them captive and plunder those who plundered them, says the Lord of lords.

On that day I will give Gog a burial place there in Israel, the great valley east of the sea. They will block the valley and bury Gog and his entire army there. It will be called the Valley of Gog’s Destruction.
For seven months the house of Israel will bury them, and the land will be cleansed.
All the people of the land will bury them, and this will bring them renown on the day when I am glorified, says the LORD.
After seven months, men will travel continually through the land, burying those who remain in the land so that it may be cleansed.
Anyone traveling through the land who sees a human bone will set up a marker beside it until the buriers come and take it away to bury it in the Valley of Gog.
The city will be named “Mighty,” and they will cleanse the land.

But you, son of man, say to all the birds of the sky and all the wild animals: This is what the Lord of lords says: Gather and come from every place to the great sacrifice that I am preparing for you on the mountains of Israel. You will eat flesh and drink blood.
You will eat the flesh of mighty warriors and drink the blood of the rulers of the earth—of rams, fattened animals, goats, bulls, and lambs, all from Bashan.
You will eat flesh until you are full and drink blood until you are drunk, from the sacrifice that I am preparing for you.
At my table you will eat your fill of the flesh of horses and their riders, of mighty warriors and all the fighting men, says the Lord of lords.
I will establish my glory among the nations, and all the nations will see the judgment I have carried out and the hand I have laid upon them.
The house of Israel will know that I am the Lord their God, from that day onward.

The nations will know that the Israelites were taken captive because of their wrongdoing, because they acted wickedly against me. I turned my face away from them and handed them over to their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.
I repaid them according to their uncleanness and their wrongdoing, and I turned my face away from them.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Now I will bring back the captives of Jacob and have mercy on the whole house of Israel, and I will be zealous for my holy name.
They will bear all their shame and the wrongdoing they committed against me when they live peacefully in their land with no one to frighten them.
When I gather them from the nations and bring them back from the countries of their enemies, I will show my holiness through them in the sight of many nations.
They will know that I am the Lord their God. I sent them into captivity among the nations, and I will gather them into their own land and leave none of them there.
I will not turn my face away from them, but I will pour out my spirit upon the whole house of Israel, says the Lord of lords.

In the twenty-fifth year of our captivity, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was destroyed, on that very day the hand of the Lord came upon me.
He brought me there in a vision of God. He brought me to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain. On its southern side was something like the buildings of a city.
He brought me there, and I saw a man whose appearance was like bronze. He had a linen cord and a measuring rod in his hand, and he was standing in the gateway.

That man said to me: Son of man, look with your eyes, listen with your ears, and take to heart everything I show you, because you have come here so that I may show it to you. Tell the Israelites everything you see.
I saw a wall surrounding that temple. The measuring rod in the man’s hand was six cubits and a handbreadth long. He measured the thickness of the structure: one rod, and its height: one rod.
He came to the gate facing east, climbed its steps, and measured the threshold of the gate: one measuring rod wide, and the other threshold one measuring rod wide.
The porch was one measuring rod long and one measuring rod wide. Between the porches were five cubits, and the threshold of the gate, inward from the gate's porches, was one measuring rod.
He measured the vestibule of the gate: eight cubits. The gate's inner threshold was two cubits.
Inside the eastern gate were three chambers on one side and three on the other. All three had the same measurements, and the porches on either side had the same measurements.
He measured the width of the gate's entrance: ten cubits; and the length of the gate: thirteen cubits.
The barrier in front of the threshold was one cubit on each side, and its interior was six cubits on this side and six cubits on that side.
He measured the gateway from roof to roof: twenty-five cubits wide, with one entrance opposite the other.
He made the space in front of the gateway sixty cubits, and the space in front of the other, outer gateway sixty cubits.
In front of the inner gateway were fifty cubits.
There were windows, broad on the inside and narrow on the outside, over the [?] and over the gate's porches. They had windows all around on the inside.
He brought me into the outer courtyard, and I saw steps all around: thirty steps, one above another.
The steps beside the gateway were opposite the length of the steps.
He measured its width from in front of the courtyard gateway: one hundred cubits to the east and to the north.
He measured the length and width of the gateway in front of him on the north side of the courtyard.
Its measurements, with three on one side and three on the other, were like those of the first gate: fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
Its windows and porches had the same measurements as those of the gate facing east. Seven steps led up to it, and there was a vestibule in front of them.
The gateways of the inner courtyard were opposite the gateway to the north and east. He measured one hundred cubits from gateway to gateway.
He led me toward the south, and I saw the southern gate. He measured its porches and its pillars according to these measurements.
It and its porches had windows all around, like these windows. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
Seven steps led up to it, and there was a vestibule in front of it. It had palm trees on its porches, one on either side.
The gateways of the inner courtyard were toward the south. He measured one hundred cubits from gateway to gateway.
He brought me into the inner courtyard through the southern gateway and measured the southern gateway according to these measurements.
Its interior, its porches, and its vestibules had these same measurements. It and its porches had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
Its walls surrounded it; they were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.
The porticoes of the outer courtyard had palm trees in them, and they had eight steps.
He brought me into the inner courtyard from the east and measured the gateway according to these measurements.
Its interior, its porches, and its vestibules—and it and its porches had windows all around—were fifty cubits in length and twenty-five in width.
The threshold of the outer courtyard; there were palm trees in the porticoes on either side, and it had eight steps.
He brought me to the northern gateway and measured it according to these measurements.
Its interior, its porches, and its vestibules, with windows all around it: its length was fifty cubits and its width twenty-five.
And the porches of the outer courtyard. There were palm trees on the porches on either side, and it had eight steps.
There was a hall whose entrance was in the gateway’s portico, and there they placed the whole burnt offerings.
In the gate's porches were two tables on one side and two tables on the other, on which to slaughter whole burnt offerings, offerings, and sacrifices for purification from sins.
At the side of the northern gate, outside the whole burnt offerings, were two tables, and on the other side of the porch were two tables.
There were four tables on one side and four tables on the other in the gate's porches: eight tables on which they slaughtered the sacrifices.

There were four tables of cut stone for the whole burnt offerings, each a cubit and a half long and a cubit and a half wide. On them they placed the instruments with which they slaughtered the whole burnt offerings and the sacrifices.
Their rims were a handbreadth wide all around, and on the tables they placed the meat of the offerings.
Outside the inner gate were chambers for the officials in the inner courtyard, beside the northern gate, facing south. One was beside the eastern gate, facing north.
He said to me, “This chamber facing south is for the priests who carry out the duties of the temple.
The hall facing north was for the priests, the descendants of Zadok, who keep charge of the altar. They are the ones among the descendants of Levi who approach to perform the service of the Lord.
He measured the courtyard: a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide, a square. The altar stood in front of the house.

He brought me to the vestibule of the house and measured the vestibule: five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other. The width of the gateway was three cubits on one side and three cubits on the other.
The vestibule was twenty cubits long and eleven cubits wide. Steps led up to it, and columns stood at the porches, one on either side.
He brought me into the sanctuary and measured the porch: six cubits wide on one side and six cubits wide on the other, and the width of the tabernacle.
The entrance was ten cubits wide, and the sides of the entrance were five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other. He measured its length as forty cubits and its width as twenty cubits.
He went inside and measured the doorway: two cubits; the gate: six cubits; and its width: seven cubits.
He measured its length as twenty cubits and its width as twenty cubits, opposite the sanctuary, and said to me, "This is the Holy of Holies."
He measured the wall of the temple: six cubits. The side chamber was seven cubits wide, all around the temple.
The side chambers were one above another, thirty-three times, and entered the wall of the temple’s side chambers all around, so that they would be supported yet remain separate from the wall.

These side chambers extended upward, winding around the temple above, so that the temple widened toward the top. From the lower chambers they would go up to the middle ones, and from the middle ones to the upper ones.
I saw the height of the temple all around. The side chambers were separated from one another by a full reed, six cubits.
The outer wall of the side chamber was five cubits thick, and the inner wall was five cubits thick.
Between the chambers surrounding the house, the width was twenty cubits.
The side chamber had doorways opening onto the space left clear, one toward the south and one toward the north. The space left clear was five cubits wide.
The building facing the separate area at the western gate was seventy cubits wide. The wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
He measured the temple: a hundred cubits long. The separate area of the walled building was a hundred cubits long.
The width in front of the temple and the eastern separate area was a hundred cubits.
He measured the length of the building facing the separate area, behind it, and its walls on either side: a hundred cubits; also the inner sanctuary and the porches of the courtyard gate.
He covered the thresholds, windows, and walls surrounding all three gates with wood all around, along its length as far as the windows.
The windows were covered above the doors of the inner temple and on the outside. He measured all the walls all around, outside and inside.
He made cherubim and palm trees, with a palm tree between one cherub and another, and each cherub had two faces.
A human face faced the palm trees on either side. This was done throughout the house, all around.
From the ground to above the doorways, cherubim and palm trees were made.
The wall of the temple was on the west, and the front of the sanctuary had the appearance

It had the appearance of a wooden altar, three cubits high and two cubits long. It had horns, and its length and its walls were of wood. He said to me, “This is the table that stands before the Lord.”
And there were two doors for each folding doorway,
two for one folding doorway and two for the other folding doorway.
On them, on the doors of the sanctuary, cherubim and palm trees were made, like those made on the walls. The front of the porch was covered with wood on the outside.
There were recessed windows and palm trees on either side, along the sides of the porch, and the side chambers of the temple were covered with boards.
He brought me out into the outer courtyard toward the north and brought me into the rooms facing the separate area and the northern building.
opposite the length of [?] cubits at the northern gate, and fifty cubits wide,
They faced the gate of the inner courtyard and the steps of the outer courtyard, and were built one above another in three stories.
In front of the rooms was a walkway ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long. The entrance to the walkway faced north.
The upper chambers were smaller because the steps extended into them.
For they were in three stories, and they had no pillars like the pillars of the courtyard. For this reason they were smaller than the lower and middle rooms.
The outer wall opposite the chambers was fifty cubits long.
For the length of the chambers of the outer courtyard was fifty cubits, while those opposite the temple were a hundred cubits long.
And the doorway of the chamber at the eastern entrance led into the outer courtyard.
Along the width of the courtyard wall, at the eastern entrance, in front of the separate area and in front of the building, were chambers.
There was a path in front of them. The appearance of the rooms toward the north, their length as well as their width, all their exits and entrances, their appearance, and their doors
were like the doors of the rooms toward the south. There was a doorway at the head of the path, the path in front of the wall toward the eastern valley, as one entered.

He said to me, “The northern rooms and the southern rooms facing the separate area are the rooms where the priests who approach the Lord eat the most holy offerings. There they place the most holy offerings, the fine flour, and the offering for purification from sins, because it is a holy place.

When the priests enter, they must not go out from the sanctuary into the outer courtyard without leaving there the garments in which they minister, because they are holy. They must put on other garments and present offerings on behalf of the people.”
He finished measuring the inner house and brought me out by way of the gate facing east, and he measured it all around.
He measured the eastern side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds.
He measured the north side with the measuring rod: five hundred rods all around.
He measured the south side: five hundred rods with the measuring rod.
He measured the western side: five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.
He measured it on its four sides. It had a wall all around, five hundred long and five hundred wide, to separate the holy from the ordinary.
He brought me to the gate facing east.
And look, the glory of the God of Israel was coming from the east. His voice was like the sound of mighty waters, and the earth shone with his glory.
It was like the vision I saw when I came to destroy the city, and like the vision I saw by the River Chebar. I fell facedown.
The glory of the Lord entered the temple through the gate facing east.
The Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner courtyard, and I saw that the glory of the Lord filled his temple.
I heard someone speaking to me from inside the temple, while the man stood beside me.

He said to me, “Son of man, this is the place of my throne and the place for the soles of my feet, where I will dwell among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel will no longer defile themselves, and they and their kings will no longer defile my holy name by their prostitution, by the corpses of their kings, and by their idols.

They placed their doorways beside my doorways and their thresholds beside my thresholds, with only a wall between me and them. They defiled my holy name by the wickedness they committed, and I destroyed them in my anger.
