Now let them remove their prostitution and the corpses of their kings from my presence, and I will dwell among them forever.
But you, son of man, show this temple to the house of Israel, so that they may be ashamed of the wickedness they committed against me. Let them measure its design.

If they are ashamed of what they have done, show them the temple’s plans, its arrangement, its entrances and exits, its entire design, all its laws, and all its plans. Write these down before their eyes, so that they may observe all its plans and its entire design and carry them out.
This is the vision of the temple: on the mountaintop, its entire surrounding territory is most holy.

These are the measurements of the altar in cubits, each cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth. Its base is a cubit by a cubit, and the border of its ledge is a span all around, and likewise on its side.
From the ground to the lower ledge is two cubits, and its width is one cubit. From the lower ledge to the upper one is four cubits, and its width is a cubit.
The altar hearth was four cubits high, and four horns rose above the hearth.
The altar hearth was twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide, square on its four sides.
Its ledge is fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide on its four sides. Its ledge and the border surrounding it are half a cubit, and it has a base all around. Its steps face east.
He said to me, “Son of man, this is what the Lord of lords says: These are the regulations for the altar on the day it is made, for offering burnt offerings on it and pouring blood on it.
You shall give the priests and Levites descended from Zadok, who approach me to serve me, says the Lord of lords, a young bull for purification from sins.
You shall take some of its blood and sprinkle it on the altar’s four horns, on the four corners of its ledge, and on the border surrounding it. You shall sprinkle it, and it will be purified.
Take the bull for the cleansing offering, and they shall burn it beside the temple, outside the sanctuary.
On the second day, offer a male goat without blemish for purification, and they shall purify the altar as they purified it with the bull.
When you have finished purifying it, offer a young bull without blemish and a ram from the flock without blemish.
Offer them before the Lord. The priests shall put salt on them and offer them as whole burnt offerings to the Lord.
For seven days you shall offer one male goat each day for purification. They shall offer one young bull and a ram from the flock without blemish for seven days.
They shall purify the altar and consecrate themselves.
When the days are completed, from the seventh day onward, the priests shall offer their whole burnt offerings and their offerings on the altar, and I will accept them, says the Lord of lords.”
He brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, which faces east, and I saw that it was shut.
The Lord said to me, “This gate shall remain shut and shall not be opened. No one shall enter through it, because the Lord, the God of Israel, has entered through it. It shall remain shut.
The ruler shall sit in it and eat bread before the Lord. He shall enter by way of the gate’s threshold and leave by the same way.”
He brought me by way of the northern gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the temple was filled with the glory of the Lord, and I fell facedown.

The Lord said to me, “Son of man, pay attention, look with your eyes, and listen with your ears to everything I tell you, to all the temple’s laws and all its forms. Pay attention to the entrances of the temple and the exits of the sanctuary.
Say to the rebellious house of Israel: This is what the Lord of lords says: Has all your defilement not been enough for you, house of Israel?

You also bring in foreigners who are uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh. They stay in my sanctuary and defile my temple while you offer my food, the fat and the blood. You break my covenant with all your defilement.
You do not fulfill the duties of my sanctuary. Instead, you have appointed your own guards to keep watch over my sanctuary.
This is what the Lord of lords says: No foreigner who is uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh shall enter my sanctuary—not even a foreigner living among the Israelites.
Nor shall the Levites who turned away from me when the Israelites strayed from me after their idols. They shall bear their guilt.
They were in my sanctuary and served at the temple gate. They shall slaughter the people’s whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, and they shall stand before them and serve them.
Because they served them before their idols and became a stumbling block of wrongdoing to the Israelites, I have raised my hand against them, says the Lord of lords, and they shall bear their guilt.
They shall not approach me to serve me, nor shall they approach any of my holy things in the Most Holy Place. They shall bear all their shame and all the defilement they have committed.
I will make them responsible for the care of the temple and for doing all the work that takes place in it.

But the priests and Levites, the descendants of Zadok, who kept charge of my sanctuary when the Israelites strayed from me, shall approach me to serve me. They shall stand before me and offer me fat and blood, says the Lord of lords.
They shall enter my sanctuary, and they shall approach my table to serve me and carry out their duties to me.
When they enter the gate of the inner courtyard, they shall wear linen garments and shall not wear wool when they serve at the gate of the inner courtyard and also inside.
They shall put linen turbans on their heads and tie linen undergarments around their waists.

When they go out to the outer courtyard to the people, they shall take off the clothes in which they minister and leave them in the sacred portico. They shall put on other clothes so that they do not make the people holy through their clothes.
They shall not shave their heads or let their hair grow long, but shall keep the hair on their heads trimmed.
The priests must not drink wine when they enter the inner courtyard.
They shall not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but only a virgin descended from Israel, or a widow whose deceased husband was a priest.
They shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and make known to them the difference between the unclean and the clean.
They shall preside over disputes as judges and judge according to my judgments. They shall observe my laws and commandments at all my appointed festivals, and they shall keep my Sabbaths holy.
They shall not go near a dead person and become unclean, except that they may become unclean for a father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or virgin sister who has not married.
After he becomes defiled, he must count seven days for himself, and then he will be purified.
On the day he enters the sanctuary, into the inner courtyard, to minister in the holy place, he shall present his purification offering, says the Lord of lords.
They shall have an inheritance: I myself am their inheritance. You shall give them no portion in Israel; I myself am their portion.
They shall eat the fine flour and the purification offering for sins, and everything devoted in Israel shall belong to them.
The best of all the firstfruits, of every contribution you set apart, shall belong to the priests. Give the first of your dough to the priests, so that a blessing may rest on your houses.
The priests must not eat any bird or animal that has been strangled or torn apart.

When you divide the land, set apart a contribution for the Lord and consecrate it from the land. Its length shall be twenty-five thousand and its width ten thousand, and its entire territory within its surrounding boundaries shall be holy.
There shall be an area for the sanctuary, five hundred by five hundred, square on all sides, with fifty cubits of open space around it.
Of this measured area, the length shall be twenty-five thousand and the width ten thousand, and within it shall be the Most Holy Place.
The holy portion of the land shall belong to the priests who minister in the Lord’s sanctuary and approach to serve the Lord. They shall have a place for houses and a holy place for the sanctuaries.
It shall be twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide, and it shall be an inheritance for the Levites who serve in the temple: twenty houses.
The city’s property shall be five thousand wide and twenty-five thousand long, alongside the allotment for the sanctuary. It shall belong to the whole house of Israel.
The ruler shall have land to the east and west of the sacred allotment and the city’s property. Its length shall correspond to one of the portions, from east to west.
It shall be an inheritance for the Israelites. The rulers of my people shall no longer oppress them, and they shall give the land to the Israelites according to their tribes.

This is what the Lord of lords says: Enough, you rulers of Israel! Put away robbery and plunder. Practice justice and righteousness, and release my people from your oppression, says the Lord of lords.
You shall have honest scales, honest measures, and honest weights.
Regulate the measure and the weight so that you take tithes fairly, one part in ten.
The weights shall be twenty [?]; a weight of them, twenty-five gerahs [?]; and a weight of fifteen shall be your mina.
Set apart this contribution: one-sixth of a cor of wheat and one-sixth of a cor of barley.
For oil, they shall take a tithe of one measure out of ten measures, which make a cor.
And one ewe out of every two hundred sheep of Israel, for the fine-flour offering, the sacrifice, and the whole burnt offering, to purify them, says the Lord of lords.
All the people of the land shall set apart this contribution for the ruler of Israel.

The ruler shall be responsible for the whole burnt offerings, the fine-flour offering, and the drink offering at the new moons, on the Sabbaths, and at all the festivals of the house of Israel. He shall present the offering for purification from sins, the fine-flour offering, the whole burnt offering, and the sacrifice that purifies the Israelites.
This is what the Lord of lords says: On the first day of the first month, take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the purification offering and sprinkle it on the thresholds of the temple, on the four corners of the altar, and on the threshold of the gate of the inner courtyard.
He shall do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who goes astray or errs, and they shall purify the temple.
On the fourteenth day of the first month, you shall observe the Passover and a festival, and for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
On that day the ruler shall present a bull as an offering for purification from sins, on behalf of himself and all the people of the land.
During the seven days of the festival, he shall present whole burnt offerings to the Lord: seven bulls and seven rams without blemish, for purification from sins, and a young goat each day.
There shall be a seah of fine flour for each bull, a seah for each ram, and a hin of oil for each seah.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, he shall observe a festival like this for seven days, with the same offering for purification from sins, the same whole burnt offerings, the same fine-flour offering, and the same oil.

This is what the Lord of lords says: The gate of the inner courtyard that faces east shall remain shut during the six days when work is done, but it shall be opened on the Sabbath day and on the day of the new moon.

The ruler shall enter from outside through the entrance at the threshold of the gate and stand at the threshold of the gate. The priests shall offer his burnt offerings and his sacrifices. He shall bow down in worship at the threshold of the gate and then leave. The gate shall not be shut until evening.
The people of the land shall bow down before the Lord at the entrance of that gate on Sabbaths and new moons.
The burnt offerings that the ruler offers before the Lord on the Sabbath day shall be six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish.
He shall provide a seah of fine flour for the bull and a seah for the ram, and for the lamb as much as he can afford, together with a hin of oil for each seah.
On the day of the new moon, he shall offer a bull without blemish, six lambs without blemish, and a ram without blemish.
He shall provide a seah of fine flour for the bull and a seah for the ram, and for the lamb as much as he can afford, together with a hin of oil for each seah.
When the ruler enters, he shall enter by the threshold of the gate and go out by the same way.

When the people of the land enter before the Lord at festival time, anyone who enters through the north gate to worship shall leave through the south gate, and anyone who enters through the south gate shall leave through the north gate. No one shall return through the gate by which he entered, but shall leave through the opposite gate.
The ruler who is among them shall go out through the gate by which he entered.
At festival time, there shall be a seah of fine flour for the bull and a seah for the ram, and for the lamb each person shall give as much as he can afford, together with a hin of oil for each seah.

When the ruler offers burnt offerings or sacrifices as a voluntary offering to the Lord, the closed gate that faces east shall be opened for him. He shall offer his burnt offerings and his sacrifices, and they shall shut the gate. Then he shall leave, as he does on the Sabbath day.
Every day, morning after morning, a year-old lamb without blemish shall be offered as a burnt offering to the Lord.
With it he shall offer fine flour every morning: one-sixth of a seah, and one-third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour. This is a lasting ordinance for the Lord, to be observed continually.
They shall offer the lambs, the fine flour, and the oil morning after morning as a continual whole burnt offering.
This is what the Lord of lords says: When the ruler gives a gift to one of his sons, his inheritance shall belong to his sons.

When he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall belong to the servant until the year of release, and then it shall belong to the ruler again. But his sons' inheritance shall remain theirs.

The ruler shall not take any of the people's inheritance or wrongfully dispossess them of their property. Instead, he shall give his sons an inheritance from his own property, so that none of my people are driven away from their inheritance.
He brought me through the entrance beside the gate into the inner portico, the holy place for the priests, which faces north. I saw that there was a place there at its far western end.

He said to me, “This is the place where the priests cook the offering for purification from sins and bake the fine flour, so that they do not bring them out into the outer courtyard and make the people holy.”
He brought me out into the outer courtyard and led me around the four sides of the courtyard. I saw a courtyard at one side of the courtyard and another courtyard at another side of the courtyard.
At the four sides of the courtyard were small courtyards, forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide.
And colonnades surrounded all four of them.
He said to me, “This is the kitchen where the servants of the temple cook the people's sacrifices.”
He brought me back to the entrance of the temple. I saw water flowing out from beneath the eastern threshold of the temple. The water was flowing down from the side of the temple, south of the altar.
He brought me out through the north gate and led me around outside to the courtyard gate that faces east. I saw water flowing out from its right side.
The glorious man went out with a measuring line in his hand. He measured a thousand cubits and led me through water that reached my ankles.
He measured a thousand cubits and led me through water that reached my knees. He measured another thousand cubits and led me through water that reached my waist.
He measured a thousand cubits, and there was a stream that no one could cross, because the water had increased and the stream had grown strong, so that no one could cross it.
He said to me, “Do you see, son of man?” Then he led me and seated me on the bank of the stream.
As I sat, I saw a great many trees on the bank of the stream, on both sides.
He said to me, “These waters flow out into eastern Galilee, descend toward the north, and enter the sea, into its foul waters, and the waters become fresh.”
Every living creature that breeds will live wherever the waters of the stream are, and there will be many fish because of those waters that flow there, and the waters will become fresh.
Fishermen will stand beside it, from En-gedi to En-eglaim. There will be places for spreading nets, and there will be many fish in it, like the fish of the Great Sea.
Its outlets and inlets will not become fresh, but will remain salt.

Along the watercourse, on its banks on both sides, every kind of tree bearing food will grow. Their leaves will not fall, and their fruit will not run out. At the beginning of every month they will bear fresh fruit, because the water they drink flows out from the sanctuary. Their fruit will be for food and their leaves for healing.
This is what the Lord of lords says: These are the boundary allotments by which the twelve tribes of Israel are to inherit the land, with a portion for Joseph.
You are to inherit it, each along with his brothers. I raised my hand in an oath to give it to your ancestors, and the land will be divided among you as an inheritance.
This is the boundary of the land on the north: from the Great Sea, along the road to Hethlon that leads to Zedad,
And Hamath, Berothah, and Sibraim, which lies between the territory of Damascus and the territory of Hamath, and Hazer-hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
The boundary will run from the sea to Hazar-enan, on the border of Damascus, and Zaphon, which is to the north, on the border of Hamath. This is the northern side.

On the eastern side, from the region of Hauran, from the region of Damascus, from the region of Gilead, and from the region of the land of Israel, the Jordan forms the boundary along the eastern sea of Tamar. This is the eastern side.
The southern side runs from Tamar as far as the waters of Meribath-kadesh, the inheritance of the Great Sea [?].
It forms the boundary as far as the point opposite the entrance to Hamath. This is the western side.
You shall divide this land among the tribes of Israel.

When you divide it as an inheritance for yourselves and for those who turn to me, who live among you and have had children among you, they will be like the Israelites. Along with you they will receive a share of the inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
In the tribe where someone who turns to me lives, there you are to give him an inheritance, says the Lord of lords.

These are the names of the tribes: from the northern extremity, along the road to Hethlon, at the entrance to Hamath and Hazar-enan, and the border of Damascus to the north beside Hamath. This is the side east of the sea belonging to Dan.
Along the border of Dan, from the eastern side to the western side, is Asher's portion.
Along the border of Asher, from the eastern side to the western side, is Naphtali's portion.
Along the border of Naphtali, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Manasseh’s portion.
Along the border of Manasseh, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Reuben’s portion.
Along the border of Reuben, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Judah’s portion.

Along the border of Judah, from the eastern side to the western side, will be the contribution you set apart, twenty-five thousand wide and as long as one of the portions. From the eastern side to the western side, the sanctuary will be in its midst.
The contribution you set apart for the Lord will be twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide.

The holy contribution will belong to the priests: twenty-five thousand on the north, with a width of ten thousand; ten thousand on the west; ten thousand on the east; and twenty-five thousand on the south. The Lord’s sanctuary will be in its midst.
It will belong to the consecrated priests descended from Zadok, who kept my requirements and did not go astray as the Israelites went astray and as the Levites went astray.
They shall have a contribution from the contribution of the land, a most holy portion adjoining the territory of the Levites.
The Levites will have land alongside the priests’ territory, twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide. Their entire territory will be twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide.
They shall not sell any of it or exchange it, nor shall they transfer the first portion of the land, because it is holy to the Lord.
The five thousand remaining along the twenty-five thousand will be a place for the city, for housing and open ground, with the city in its midst.

These are its measurements: four thousand five hundred on the northern side, four thousand five hundred on the east, four thousand five hundred on the south, and four thousand five hundred on the west.
The city’s open ground will extend two hundred fifty to the north, two hundred fifty to the south, two hundred fifty to the east, and two hundred fifty to the west.

What remains alongside the holy contribution—ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the west—will lie alongside the holy contribution. Its produce will provide food for those who work for the city.
Those who work for the city shall be drawn from all the tribes of Israel.
The entire contribution will be twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand. Set apart the holy contribution from the city’s property.

What remains will belong to the city’s ruler: from the holy contribution and the city’s property to the eastern boundary, twenty-five thousand, and to the west, twenty-five thousand at the western boundary, alongside the ruler’s portion. The holy contribution and the sanctuary of the temple will be in its midst.
From the Levites’ inheritance and from the city’s inheritance, the ruler’s portion will be in the city, between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin.
As for the remaining tribes, from the eastern side to the western side shall be Benjamin’s portion.
Along the border of Benjamin, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Simeon’s portion.
Along the border of Simeon, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Issachar’s portion.
Along the border of Issachar, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Zebulun’s portion.
Along the border of Zebulun, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Gad’s portion.
Along the border of Gad, on the southern side, the boundary will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, its inheritance extending to the Great Sea.
This is the land you are to divide as an inheritance among the tribes of Israel, and these are their portions, says the Lord of lords.
These are the exits of the city: on the northern side, the measurement shall be four thousand five hundred.
The city’s gates will bear the names of the tribes of Israel. On the north there will be three gates: one for Reuben, one for Judah, and one for Levi.
On the east, the measurement will be four thousand five hundred, with three gates: one for Joseph, one for Benjamin, and one for Dan.
On the south side, the measurement is four thousand five hundred, with three gates: one for Simeon, one for Issachar, and one for Zebulun.
On the west side, the measurement is four thousand five hundred, with three gates: one for Gad, one for Asher, and one for Naphtali.
Its perimeter shall be eighteen thousand, and the name of the city from that time on shall be “The Lord Is There.”
